title: New York's Fifth Avenue Reclaims World's Most Expensive Retail Street Ranking | Cushman & Wakefield
summary: Read Cushman & Wakefield's Main Streets Across the World 2026 report.
body_markdown:
New York's Fifth Avenue


*Global prime retail rents rise 3% as demand for flagship locations remains strong despite economic uncertainty.*


**[New York](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-states/offices/new-york) – November 17, 2026** – New York City's Upper Fifth Avenue has reclaimed its position as the world's most expensive[retail](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/industries/retail) street, according to Cushman & Wakefield's[Main Streets Across the World 2026](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/insights/main-streets-across-the-world) report. Rents along the corridor increased 35% over the past year to $2,700 per square foot (psf) annually, moving the destination from third place in 2025 to first for the first time since 2023.


[London's](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-kingdom/offices/london-city) New Bond Street ranked second at $2,230 psf annually, followed by[Milan's](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/italy/offices/milan-filippo-turati) Via Montenapoleone at $2,160 psf. Both streets recorded flat rental growth over the past year after significant increases in prior years.


The annual report, which examines headline rents across 147 leading retail locations globally, found that rents increased an average of 3.0% year-over-year in local currency terms. While growth moderated from 4.3% in 2025, nearly half (49%) of the streets surveyed recorded rental increases, compared with 19% that experienced declines. The remaining 32% held steady.


"While rental growth has moderated globally, competition for space in the world's most established retail destinations remains intense," said Dr. Dominic Brown, Head of International Research, Global Think Tank at Cushman & Wakefield. "The return of Fifth Avenue to the top of the rankings demonstrates how quickly rents can accelerate when strong retailer demand meets limited availability. We are seeing similar dynamics across major global markets, where retailers continue to prioritize locations that offer international visibility, strong consumer spending and long-term brand value."


The Americas and Asia Pacific recorded the strongest regional rental growth at 3.1%, followed by Europe at 2.9%. Asia Pacific was the only region to experience an acceleration in rental growth, up from 2.3% in 2025.


### Retailers Continue to Compete for Limited Prime Space


Despite a challenging global economic environment, leasing activity across the world's leading retail destinations remains strong. Cushman & Wakefield recorded more than 815,000 square feet of leasing activity across the top 30 retail streets, representing 153 new leases and store openings. More than 80% of that activity involved retailers new to their respective streets, while international brands accounted for approximately 90% of space leased.


Fashion retailers remained the largest source of demand, accounting for 50% of leasing transactions and 57% of space taken. However, health and beauty, personal goods, food and beverage, and experiential retail concepts are contributing to a broader mix of tenants in traditionally fashion-dominated locations.


The report also found that vacancy remains exceptionally limited across many of the world's most sought-after retail streets, with most recording low single-digit vacancy rates and some reporting no available space.


"Retailers are becoming increasingly selective about where they grow, but competition for premier locations has never been more intense,” said Alanna Loeffler, Senior Managing Director, Americas Retail Platform Lead at Cushman & Wakefield. "Today’s flagship store is more than a place to transact, it is a brand-building platform that drives visibility, customer engagement and long-term loyalty. As a result, demand continues to concentrate in a relatively small number of global retail destinations, while a new generation of mixed-use districts is emerging as retailers follow growth in tourism, affluence and consumer spending.”


### Retail Demand Expands Beyond Traditional Gateway Cities


While New York, London, Paris, Milan and Tokyo remain central to international retail expansion, the report identifies growing demand across additional urban retail districts.


In the United States,[Miami's](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-states/offices/miami) Brickell Boulevard Corridor recorded a 43% increase in rents, while Austin's South Congress rose 20%. In Asia Pacific, Mumbai's Linking Road recorded 28% growth, reflecting strong demand for premium retail space in India. Across Europe, Bucharest's Calea Victoriei recorded a 29% increase, while London's Covent Garden and Regent Street each experienced 13% growth.
These trends reflect the growing importance of mixed-use retail districts, where residential development, hospitality, dining, entertainment and office activity support consumer traffic and retailer demand.


Looking ahead, Cushman & Wakefield expects competition for limited prime retail space to remain a defining feature of the market. Retailers are also increasingly incorporating artificial intelligence into customer engagement, inventory management and store operations, further integrating digital capabilities with the physical shopping experience.


"The strongest retail destinations are continuing to evolve as brands rethink how they engage with consumers," Brown added. "While technology is changing how people discover and purchase products, physical stores remain essential to brand identity and customer experience. Locations that can support those objectives will continue to attract demand, even as economic conditions and consumer spending patterns shift."
